aboutlead: A useful solution starts with understanding the question.
aboutparagraphs: I am a Full Professor of Statistics and Operations Research at Universidad Miguel Hernández de Elche, Deputy Director of i-MInD and Director of the UMH–FISABIO Joint Research Unit on Statistical Methods in Health Sciences.

My work combines machine learning, Bayesian modelling, spatial analysis and efficiency assessment. I collaborate with specialists in health, the environment, industry and economics to turn data into evidence and useful tools.
Knowledge transfer is part of this approach to research: developing methods, validating them in context and working with the people who will use them.
careeritems: PhD from UMH in 2009, researching geostatistical models for bioclimatic indices. Statistics degrees from Universidad de Alicante and UMH.
Chair of the International Biometric Society Representative Council and ex officio member of its Executive Board, 2026–2027.
Member of the Executive Committee of the Spanish Society of Biostatistics.
Deputy Vice-Rector for Research at UMH, 2011–2023. Editorial and peer-review activity, including statistical editing for Public Health Nutrition.
researchtitle: The method matters. So does the application.
researchintro: Machine learning, uncertainty and models that connect disciplines. Selected work with links to the original publications.
paperdescs: Generative AI for clinical recommendations: a proof-of-concept study using a closed evidence corpus.
Adapting Random Forest to estimate production technologies and measure efficiency in education.
Machine learning to model species distributions on a global scale.
A machine-learning calculator to predict musculoskeletal injuries in surgeons.
A review of Bayesian networks for disease diagnosis and prognosis.
Open-source R software for fitting Efficiency Analysis Trees.
projectsintro: Experience with specific problems across different sectors. These examples illustrate areas of work, rather than an exhaustive list of collaborations.
projecttexts: Development and validation of predictive models for repeat-offence risk assessment within the ALTEA project. Statistics and AI to support police risk assessment tools.

Selected success stories include predicting musculoskeletal risk in surgeons and analysing acceptance of remote consultations. Examples from a wider track record in clinical studies, treatment evaluation and predictive tools.
Thermal risk in aquaculture, species distributions and environmental data integration. Maps and models to inform management and adaptation.
Compost Calculator, sludge characterisation, waste valorisation, irrigation and soil zoning. Analysis to evaluate processes and resource-use options.
Turf management, fertilisation and remote sensing. Evidence to inform maintenance and resource use.
Experimental design, formulation, preservation and consumer preferences. Comparing products, processes and coproduct ingredients.
partnertext: I collaborate with Juan Aparicio and other research teams on methodological development and knowledge transfer projects. Sector knowledge and collaboration across disciplines are part of every solution.
humanintro: Useful AI must pay attention both to model quality and to the people it affects.
humantext: My experience in risk assessment, health research and large-scale citizen surveys connects methods with social needs. I see AI as a tool to support informed decisions, with human oversight and attention to its limitations.
principles: Explain what a model answers, which data it uses and what it assumes.
Make uncertainty visible and assess where a tool works.
Consider bias and the consequences of using the results.
Support professional judgement and the responsibility of decision-makers.
ethicstitle: Ethics and integrity in scientific practice
ethicstext: Biostatistical member of the UMH Animal Experimentation Ethics Committee and Research Ethics and Integrity Committee since September 2026.
trainingtitle: Understand AI. Put it to better use.
trainingintro: Specialised training to help teams understand tools, interpret results and apply them with judgement in their work.
courses: Generative AI, document analysis, security and practical applications for more efficient public administration.
Data science and machine learning to analyse information and evaluate predictive models.
Experimental design, methodology and statistical analysis, including training in animal experimentation.
Teaching innovation, digital skills and contributions to postgraduate and digital health training.
teachingnote: University teaching since 2005, specialised training and Teaching Talent recognition. Excellent evaluations in DOCENTIA-UMH.
personalintro: I am from Dénia. Cycling and playing the dolçaina are two ways to switch off, enjoy myself and spend time with others.
biketitle: Another way to explore the road ahead.

rowingnote: Rowing is also part of my story, although I am currently taking a break from it.
